Yes. The subtext enriches the setting rather than feeling forced. Ilse’s remark “Und dazwischen? … Bin ich” makes her both a literal crossing point and an embodiment of the ferry’s enduring place in local life. The fog, cold, and repetitive crossings suggest isolation and accumulated weariness without explicitly naming them.

Her hesitation before the Munich phone call also implies emotional distance or unresolved tension with Jonas. His knowledge of her crossing schedule contrasts with her dismissive description of his consulting work, suggesting shared history alongside estrangement. These implications emerge naturally from ordinary actions and restrained dialogue.
